definitions.explanation: To show signs of disliking something; to express unwillingness or reluctance. Used when describing someone else's feelings of aversion.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{野菜|やさい}を{嫌|いや}がる。
{猫|ねこ}は{水|みず}を{嫌|いや}がることが{多|おお}い。
{彼|かれ}は{人前|ひとまえ}で{話|はな}すのを{嫌|いや}がっている。
examples.english: He is reluctant to speak in front of people.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{嫌|いや}がる.

GRAMMAR POINT:
{嫌|いや}がる is formed from {嫌|いや} (disliked) + がる (to show signs of). The がる suffix indicates observable behavior showing an internal feeling, used when describing others' feelings (not your own).

ASPECT: {嫌|いや}がっている indicates ongoing reluctance or aversion.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嫌|いや}がる: to show dislike (observable behavior)
- {嫌|きら}う: to dislike (internal feeling, can be used for self)
- {嫌|いや}だ: to dislike (direct statement of own feelings)
